title: Does rotor cant still pay once a co-designed quadrotor must hold position?
lede: once the vehicle must hold position, does a canted-rotor quadrotor still win? In simulation cant still buys yaw (−6° RMS, 5 of 5 seeds) but not position, and the sideways force a tilted rotor makes under roll/pitch torque breaks designs tuned without it (1.1 m against 0.25 m position error).
summary: Five earlier codesign-aero-cant* projects deferred position hold. Here the quadrotor gets translation, an outer position loop and the body-lateral force of a canted rotor, F = τ tan α / r per unit commanded roll or pitch torque (closed form checked against an explicit four-rotor allocation). Joint CMA-ES over arm length, propeller size, cant and nine gains (3200 evaluations, 5 seeds, 64 held-out episodes). Cant still cuts yaw error by 5.8° (bound 35°) and 6.0° (bound 80°), better in 5 of 5 paired seeds, while position error is unchanged within noise (0.25 m against 0.22 m with no cant). Designs tuned with the lateral force switched off and then scored with it on reach 1.1–1.2 m position error, worse in 5 of 5 seeds; the force acts as a disturbance (switching it off improves force-aware designs), with an unhelpful sign on the roll axis for this layout. Limits: 2 s episodes, objective weights (0.1 m against 10°) chosen, several seeds stop in local optima, one arm layout, perfect altitude hold; cost model, noise, offset and plant ranges are assumed or inherited, not measured; no hardware.
why_standalone: Next step of the existing codesign-aero-cant chain (five sibling READMEs defer exactly this); no codesign programme exists yet, and folding the 26 codesign-* directories into one is a separate consolidation.
